parts.note: nerve that comes out of a container of gin, and slang for nerve itself

explanation.surface: A question about the bravery drink is said to give.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bottle' means nerve, and Dutch courage is the boldness got from drink, which comes in a bottle; the question mark flags the double sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch courage is boldness from alcohol, and the slang word for nerve is also the vessel the spirit is poured from.

clue.text: She may have been banned for changing her name

definitions.text: She may have been banned for changing her name

parts.words: She may have been banned for changing her name
parts.note: 'banned' read as having banns read, the notice of a coming wedding

explanation.surface: A woman forbidden from altering her name.
explanation.walkthrough: Banns are the church notice of an intended marriage; a woman who has had banns read is about to take a new surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman about to marry, whose banns are read and who often takes her husband's surname.

definitions.meaning: leaving the ground in an aircraft

explanation.surface: Launch a plane from the airstrip.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a parody (a send-up) and an aircraft leaving the ground.

clue.text: Aspirations of those after superior positions

definitions.text: Aspirations of those after superior positions

parts.words: Aspirations of those after superior positions
parts.note: 'superior' read as high up: goals that are elevated

explanation.surface: The ambitions of people seeking promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: High ambitions, those of someone set on reaching elevated rank.

definitions.meaning: to call in or go past, as in dropping by a friend's house

explanation.surface: Get hold of a ticket or permit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both acquire (come by a fortune) and drop in on or go past (come by later).

clue.text: True love can prove so extravagant

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: may turn out to be something else, so the letters before are remade

explanation.surface: A romance that turns out over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can prove' rearranges TRUE with O; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional and beyond the bounds of propriety, bizarrely exaggerated.

clue.text: Mike's so upset by cold foreigners

indicators.note: knocked over, so the letters of the words before tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone named Mike is disturbed by chilly outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MIKESSO; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit peoples of the Arctic, living in a freezing climate.

parts.note: 'local' as a British pub; an old-fashioned quantity of beer

explanation.surface: An obsolete unit used in one district.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British neighbourhood pub; this tall trumpet-shaped glass holds about two and a half pints.
explanation.definitionFit: A long horn-shaped drinking glass, now a pub novelty, once a measure of beer.

clue.text: Record attendance of pupils for lecture

definitions.meaning: marking each name on the register as present

explanation.surface: A teacher takes the register before a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; the second sense is the informal British use, to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking names on a register is checking them off with a mark, and the informal phrase also means to rebuke.

parts.note: read not as fire engines but as people who look after a furnace

explanation.surface: Fire engines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire tenders' suggests fire engines; read literally it is people who tend a fire, as on a steam ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who shovel coal into and look after a furnace or boiler.

definitions.meaning: taken apart, as a tent or scaffolding

explanation.surface: Logged as taken apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means written down (notes taken) and also dismantled, as scaffolding is.

parts.note: 'way' read as a road, a lane where one goes back over the past

explanation.surface: A technique for recall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' looks like method but is a road: a trip down this lane is nostalgia.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip down this imaginary lane is reminiscing about the past, and a lane is a way.

definitions.meaning: a member of a people of north-west Africa

explanation.surface: Barren ground in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moor is a North African Muslim of Berber and Arab descent; a moor is open heathland.

clue.text: Plain clothes expert in Moslem law

definitions.meaning: civilian dress worn by one usually in uniform
a Muslim legal scholar who issues rulings

explanation.surface: An Islamic jurist out of uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both civilian dress worn off duty and a Muslim scholar who gives legal opinions (fatwas).

clue.text: Keeps on, showing stamina in trouble

indicators.note: being in trouble means being disturbed, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going, showing endurance in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder: 'trouble' rearranges STAMINA and IN; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep up or continue something, as in sustaining a pace.

indicators.note: playful and lively, so the letters of the next word jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: Playful mythical horse-men from before Roman times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisky' rearranges CENTAURS. The Etruscans ruled much of Italy before Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruria was the civilisation of central Italy that preceded and influenced Rome.

definitions.meaning: to dash from one side to the other

explanation.surface: Hurry across the road to greet someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to dash over a space and to encounter someone unexpectedly.

definitions.meaning: set out or placed in order

explanation.surface: Feeling inclined while getting organised.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means inclined (well disposed) and also placed or set out in order.

clue.text: An error in the wage packet?

definitions.text: An error in the wage packet?

parts.words: An error in the wage packet?
parts.note: 'slip' read as a mistake, though it is the printed note of earnings

explanation.surface: A mistake in someone's wages.
explanation.walkthrough: A slip is a mistake and also a strip of paper; the slip in the wage packet shows the pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The note of earnings and deductions enclosed with wages.

clue.text: When it reacts saltpetre may be extracted

indicators.note: letters can be drawn out from inside the phrase before, like a chemical from a solution

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson on getting saltpetre from a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be extracted' picks letters running across 'wheN IT REacts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, traditionally called nitre.

indicators.note: re-formation, forming the word again in a new shape

explanation.surface: Defeat the Catholic revival of the 16th century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformation' is read as re-forming: it rearranges COUNTER; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to defeat heavily.

definitions.meaning: to halt or delay, as in a ... of execution
a prop or brace, as a ship's rope or corset bone

explanation.surface: Look at the supporting structure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to halt or postpone and also a rope or prop that holds something up.

parts.note: 'air' read as a tune: the song of birds at daybreak

explanation.surface: The fresh atmosphere at sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' suggests the atmosphere; here it is a melody, the birdsong at first light.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds sing together most at first light, a tune heard at daybreak.

indicators.note: made again in a new shape, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Claud mends his ways gracefully.
explanation.walkthrough: A duke is addressed as 'Your Grace', so a ducal person is one with that title.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a duke, a nobleman styled 'His Grace'.

parts.note: pressing read as pressing someone to act, not ironing

explanation.surface: Ironed clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' suggests ironing; it is persuading.
explanation.definitionFit: Encouraged strongly, pressed someone to act.

clue.text: Due to a small rise, I'll get in some wine

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, the I'll entering the wine

parts.note: hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Someone blames a small price rise for the wine they are buying in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Due to' is a link. HOCK is the British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillock is a little hill, a small rise in the ground.

parts.note: money in metal form rather than notes

explanation.surface: Ready money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' suggests ready or actual cash; here it is literal: metal money.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal pieces of currency are literally hard money, as opposed to paper notes.

parts.note: bending readily, like a pliant reed rather than a persuadable mind

explanation.surface: Readily persuaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swayed' suggests persuaded; read physically it is bending without breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant and flexible, bending readily without breaking.

indicators.note: disturbed or disconcerted, so the letters of the word before are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone declines to extinguish a glass of port, or a harbour stays lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges DOESNT. Ostend is a Belgian port with ferries to England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian ferry harbour on the North Sea coast.
